newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - CIPS March report on services.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - CIPS March report on services.

text.p: Following is a list of economists' reactions to the new survey by the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply on the Britain's service industries. The business activity index rose to 63.3 in March, up from 60.4 in February.

"It sounds pretty punchy. This is the party of the economy which is growing quite quickly and I'm concerned about cost pressures here. The ONS has tried to monitor the service sector more carefully but we still know relatively little about it."

"This is a welcome addition, given lack of official data. It does certainly confirm the impression that the service sector is very strong and it is worrying that it is getting stronger. This will be more evidence used by the governor to press the new Chancellor of the Exchequer to tighten policy after the election. The prices information show that prices charged have been above 50 since November. This is consistant with the view that inflation is picking up in the services sector, which is being masked by favourable developments in food and manufacturing prices due to the exchange rate."

"The survey's telling us the service sector continued in the first quarter of this year where it left off last year - service sector output in 1996 grew about three times faster than the production sector, and we're seeing a similar pattern so far this year. It does suggest there's going to be a lot of pressure on the new Chancellor, whoever he may be, after the election, to make an early adjustment on interest rates. It's not inflationary as such, but I think we're seeing a good parallel with the U.S. where the economy is coming up against capacity and resource constraints."
